title: Egress and request charges: why reading can cost more than storing

videos.script: Most people price a bucket by its size. That is one meter of three, and often the smallest. {{meters}} Every request has a price, whatever its size. Every byte that leaves the region has a price too. Storage is only what the bucket costs while nobody touches it. {{requests}} In this lesson a short program prices four designs. One design writes every tap as its own object and reads them all every morning. It spends more than a hundred times its storage on requests. The same bytes in a hundred and twenty-three files cost almost nothing to read. {{small}} Then Quitanda's product images, served to the internet. The transfer is nearly the whole bill, and it falls in steps as the volume grows. {{tiers}} Then the traffic that never leaves AWS: between zones, to another region, and through a NAT gateway that charges for every gigabyte on its way to S3. One free endpoint takes that line off the bill. {{inside}} And requester pays, the setting that sends part of the bill to whoever asks. {{payer}}
